messages:
Maria: Quick ask — can someone run a quick pairwise perf for A100 / H100 / L40S? Longctx=32k, tiny batch=1, batchpack=4. Need p50/p95/p99 + cost estimates by EOD tomorrow for SOC review.
Ben: I can do overnight on benchpool-2. Which model? gptx-7b? Quant? Repeats?
Maria: gptx-7b, q4f16 is fine. Repeats 3, include KV warmup (2 prefix runs).
Carla: Heads up — L40S nodes are in eu-west-1 and H100s are in us-west-2. Prefer same region to avoid network variability.
Ben: Good call. I'll provision H100 in eu-west-1 ephemeral. benchbot: queued job 99827
benchbot: executing:
```bash
bench run --pool benchpool-2 --model gptx-7b --quant q4f16 --sweep "A100,H100,L40S" --seq 32768 --batch 1 --batchpack 4 --repeats 3 --kv-warmup 2 --out gs://redwood-perf/174999/99827
```
Dave: Also capture kernel fallback logs and pcie stats (nvidia-smi dmon), tag job with 'pairwise-174999'.
Ben: will do. adding nvlink & thermal tags.
Carla: If L40S shows thermal throttling, include node id and temp logs please.
benchbot: job 99827 started on 1749992222 :rocket:
Ben: quick status — H100 run done, A100 started, L40S queued. Will post raw CSVs + a 1-slide summary.
Maria: thanks. if L40S is noisy we might run a second replicate later.
benchbot: job 99827 complete. outputs -> gs://redwood-perf/174999/99827/
Ben: summary (raw): H100 p50 85ms p95 210ms p99 420ms; A100 p50 120ms p95 260ms p99 560ms; L40S p50 95ms p95 230ms p99 640ms. Notes: L40S node-3 thermal spike after 75 tokens -> 20% slowdown; A100 shows higher p99 variance. Cost (approx per 1M tokens): H100 $28, A100 $22, L40S $24.
Carla: thx — can you upload a tiny plot and attach CSV headers? also add bench config JSON.
Ben: uploaded: gs://redwood-perf/174999/99827/summary.png and /99827/bench-config.json
Maria: perfect. I'll include in the SOC pack. :thumbsup:
Dave: follow-up: create an infra ticket to check L40S cooling on node-3. tagging @infra-sig
Carla: ping infra-sig for node-3 investigation.
infra-sig: noted, creating ticket INFRA-1147, investigating thermal logs.
Maria: closing loop — great job everyone.
